subject: Information Theory
title: Computational vs Perfect Security
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Computational vs Perfect Security.

hook.text: AES-256 isn't perfectly secret. An attacker could theoretically break it. We just bet they never will.

buildup.text: Computational security assumes attackers have limited time and computing power. Perfect secrecy assumes unlimited.

discovery.text: In practice, computational security works brilliantly. No one has broken AES in over two decades.

twist.text: The gap is philosophical: perfect secrecy is provably unbreakable. Computational security is just very, very hard.

climax.text: Almost all modern cryptography is computationally secure. The one-time pad remains the only perfect option.

quiz.question: What does computational security assume?
options: Attackers have limited time and computing power
